words.enDefinition: The basic need an offering satisfies or the main outcome buyers seek.

examples.en: The team identified taking readable notes as the core benefit behind its classroom tablet concept.
examples.zh: 小组把记下清楚易读的笔记视为课堂平板概念要提供的「核心利益」。

examples.en: Our case compared two lamps with different designs but the same core benefit for students.
examples.zh: 案例比较了两款设计不同、却给学生带来相同「核心利益」的台灯。

collocations: the core benefit of the product

words.enDefinition: In the three-level product model, the offering as designed and sold, including its features, branding, quality, and packaging.

examples.en: In the kit example, the actual product included the notebook design, paper quality, and reusable case.
examples.zh: 在套装示例中，笔记本设计、纸张质量和可重复使用的外盒都属于「实体产品层」。

examples.en: We listed the actual product separately from the note-taking benefit it provided in our concept board.
examples.zh: 我们在概念板上分别列出「实体产品层」和它给使用者带来的记笔记便利。

collocations: distinguish the actual product from its core benefit

words.enDefinition: The attributes and conditions buyers normally expect with an offering in its category.

examples.en: In the classroom case, clear assembly instructions were part of the expected product for a shelving kit.
examples.zh: 课堂案例中，易懂的安装说明属于搁架套装的「期望产品层」。

examples.en: We discussed whether a secure lid belonged to the expected product in the reusable cup category.
examples.zh: 我们讨论，在可重复使用杯这一品类中，能盖紧的杯盖是否属于「期望产品层」。

collocations: a service included in the expected product

words.enDefinition: The offering with extras and services exceeding what buyers ordinarily expect.

examples.en: The case added a drawing workshop to the augmented product for students buying the art kit.
examples.zh: 案例为购买美术套装的学生提供绘画指导课，将其计入「附加产品层」。

examples.en: Our group compared the augmented product across two fictional brands selling otherwise similar study lamps.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个虚构品牌的「附加产品层」，它们所卖的学习台灯本身很相似。

collocations: services included in the augmented product
the benefits of an augmented product

words.enDefinition: Possible future improvements and additions to an offering.

examples.en: The potential product in our case included a replacement cover that the current notebook lacked.
examples.zh: 我们案例中的「潜在产品层」包括当前笔记本尚未配备的可替换封皮。

examples.en: The team put future customization ideas under the potential product on its classroom product map.
examples.zh: 小组在课堂产品示意图上，将未来可做的定制项目归入「潜在产品层」。

words.enDefinition: A characteristic of an offering that can be described, observed, or judged.

examples.en: The exercise asked which product attribute mattered most when buyers compared the two fictional bags.
examples.zh: 练习问，买家比较两款虚构包袋时，哪项「产品属性」最重要。

examples.en: The group listed a washable lining as a product attribute and easier cleaning as its benefit.
examples.zh: 小组把可洗内衬列为「产品属性」，将更方便清洁列为它带来的利益。

words.enDefinition: A practical result that helps customers accomplish something with the offering.

examples.en: The functional benefit of the folding stand was that it freed space on a small desk.
examples.zh: 可折叠支架的「功能性利益」是腾出小书桌上的空间。

examples.en: Our assignment asked us to describe a functional benefit before listing the hardware that produced it.
examples.zh: 作业要求先说明一项「功能性利益」，再列出带来该利益的硬件。

words.enDefinition: A feeling a customer gains from using or owning an offering.

examples.en: The fictional repair kit offered an emotional benefit because students felt more confident tackling small fixes.
examples.zh: 虚构工具套装让学生更有信心应付小修小补，提供了「情感利益」。

examples.en: We discussed the emotional benefit of a familiar welcome page in the case about new students.
examples.zh: 我们在新生案例中讨论了熟悉的欢迎页面带来的「情感利益」。

collocations: connect a feature to an emotional benefit

words.enDefinition: A way an offering helps customers express their identity or values.

examples.en: The self-expressive benefit of the interchangeable covers was that students could show their own design preferences.
examples.zh: 可替换封皮带来的「自我表达利益」是让学生能展现自己的设计偏好。

examples.en: We compared the self-expressive benefit of visible club badges with the practical benefit of a stronger bag.
examples.zh: 我们比较了显眼的社团徽章带来的「自我表达利益」与包袋更加结实带来的实际好处。

words.enDefinition: A specific offering within a seller's product line or overall selection.

examples.en: The catalogue counted the large sketchbook as one product item within the fictional stationery line.
examples.zh: 产品目录将大号素描本算作虚构文具线中的一项「单项产品」。

examples.en: The class marked each product item separately before totaling the items sold by the mock company.
examples.zh: 全班先分别标出各「单项产品」，再统计模拟公司销售的项目总数。

collocations: a product item in the line

words.enDefinition: A group of related offerings sold by the same organization.

examples.en: The fictional campus shop put its drawing pads and sketchbooks in a single product line.
examples.zh: 虚构校园商店将画纸本和素描本归入同一条「产品线」。

examples.en: Our group examined the product line to see where another notebook model might fit naturally.
examples.zh: 小组查看了这条「产品线」，看再加入一种笔记本型号是否合适。

words.enDefinition: The number of distinct product lines offered by a business.

examples.en: Adding a line of desk lamps increased product mix width in our fictional retail case.
examples.zh: 在虚构零售案例中，增加台灯产品线扩大了「产品组合宽度」。

examples.en: We counted the product lines rather than the individual items to calculate product mix width.
examples.zh: 我们用产品线的数量来计算「产品组合宽度」，没有逐个数其中的单项产品。

words.enDefinition: The number of versions or items offered within a particular product line.

examples.en: The fictional stationery company increased product line depth by adding two new sizes to its notebook range.
examples.zh: 虚构文具公司为笔记本系列增设两种尺寸，提高了「产品线深度」。

examples.en: Our team compared product line depth for two lamp lines with different numbers of finishes and sizes.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个台灯系列的「产品线深度」，它们各自提供的表面处理和尺寸数量不同。

words.enDefinition: The total number of individual items across all product lines.

examples.en: We calculated product mix length by adding the item counts for every line in the fictional catalogue.
examples.zh: 我们将虚构产品目录中各条产品线的项目数量相加，算出「产品组合长度」。

examples.en: Removing two notebook models reduced product mix length even though the number of lines stayed the same.
examples.zh: 尽管产品线条数没变，取消两种笔记本型号仍缩短了「产品组合长度」。

collocations: compare the product mix length of two firms

words.enDefinition: How closely related the product lines are in use, production, distribution, or another relevant dimension.

examples.en: We assessed product mix consistency by checking whether different lines used similar materials or sales outlets.
examples.zh: 我们核对各条产品线是否使用相近材料或销售网点，以评估「产品组合一致性」。

examples.en: The class discussed product mix consistency after noticing that notebooks and pencil cases served the same customers.
examples.zh: 发现笔记本和笔袋服务同一批顾客后，全班讨论了「产品组合一致性」。

collocations: compare firms on product mix consistency

words.enDefinition: Adding items within a product line's existing range of offerings.

examples.en: The case illustrated line filling by adding a medium notebook between the existing small and large models.
examples.zh: 案例在原有的小号和大号笔记本之间新增中号款，展示了「产品线填补」。

examples.en: We chose line filling because the new model would sit between the two notebooks already sold.
examples.zh: 我们选择「产品线填补」，因为新型号会介于已销售的两款笔记本之间。

words.enDefinition: Adding offerings beyond a product line's current position at one or both ends.

examples.en: The assignment compared line stretching with adding another version between the existing models in the line.
examples.zh: 作业把「产品线延伸」与在这条线的现有型号之间新增款式作比较。

examples.en: We discussed line stretching after the fictional company proposed a range aimed at a different quality tier.
examples.zh: 虚构公司提出面向不同质量档次的产品系列后，我们讨论了「产品线延伸」。

words.enDefinition: An extension that adds products above the line's existing market tier.

examples.en: The upgraded cover and paper made the premium sketchbook an upward line stretch in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 在课堂案例中，封面和纸张升级后，高端素描本成了一项「产品线向上延伸」。

examples.en: We discussed whether buyers would trust an upward line stretch from the fictional budget stationery brand.
examples.zh: 我们讨论买家是否会信任这个虚构平价文具品牌的「产品线向上延伸」。

collocations: an example of an upward line stretch

words.enDefinition: An extension that adds products below the line's existing market tier.

examples.en: The basic lamp represented a downward line stretch for a fictional brand previously selling premium models.
examples.zh: 对之前只卖高端型号的虚构品牌而言，这种基础款台灯是一次「产品线向下延伸」。

examples.en: Students debated whether a downward line stretch would change perceptions of the original desk accessory line.
examples.zh: 学生讨论「产品线向下延伸」会不会改变顾客对原来桌面用品系列的看法。

collocations: risks of a downward line stretch

words.enDefinition: Removing individual offerings from a product line to simplify or strengthen it.

examples.en: The fictional company used product line pruning to remove two versions that met almost identical needs.
examples.zh: 虚构公司通过「产品线精简」，去掉了满足几乎相同需求的两个款式。

examples.en: We considered product line pruning after most fictional customers chose the same two notebook formats.
examples.zh: 当大多数虚构顾客都选择同两种笔记本规格时，我们考虑了「产品线精简」。

collocations: the effect of product line pruning

words.enDefinition: An offering typically bought frequently with little effort or comparison.

examples.en: In our retail exercise, the shop sold individual pens near the checkout as a convenience product.
examples.zh: 零售练习中，商店在结账区附近把单支笔作为「便利品」销售。

examples.en: Students identified a convenience product when the fictional buyers spent little time comparing their familiar options.
examples.zh: 虚构买家几乎不花时间比较熟悉的选项，学生由此辨认出一种「便利品」。

collocations: classify an item as a convenience product

words.enDefinition: An offering buyers typically compare on suitability, quality, style, or price before choosing.

examples.en: Our classroom case classified a desk chair as a shopping product because students compared several models.
examples.zh: 在我们的课堂案例中，学生比较多个型号后才决定，因此书桌椅被归为「选购品」。

examples.en: The fictional buyers chose a shopping product after checking how well each model fitted their workspace.
examples.zh: 虚构买家核对各型号与学习空间的适配程度，才选定这种「选购品」。

collocations: classify an item as a shopping product

words.enDefinition: An offering for which buyers will make an unusual effort to obtain a preferred option.

examples.en: The class called it a specialty product because fictional buyers traveled specifically for that model.
examples.zh: 全班将它称作「特殊品」，因为虚构买家专程前去购买这一型号。

examples.en: We compared a specialty product with a similar item buyers would happily replace with another brand.
examples.zh: 我们把「特殊品」与一种相似商品作比较，后者的买家愿意换成其他品牌。

collocations: classify an item as a specialty product

words.enDefinition: An offering customers do not know about or ordinarily consider buying.

examples.en: The emergency repair membership was an unsought product for students who rarely thought about broken bicycles.
examples.zh: 对平时很少想到自行车会坏的学生而言，紧急维修会籍属于「非寻求品」。

examples.en: We discussed how an unfamiliar service might be an unsought product even if it met a real need.
examples.zh: 我们讨论，一项陌生服务即使满足实际需求，也可能属于「非寻求品」。

collocations: an example of an unsought product

words.enDefinition: A physical product intended to last through extended or repeated use.

examples.en: The fictional student counted the desk lamp as a durable good and expected years of use.
examples.zh: 虚构学生将台灯算作「耐用品」，预计能用好几年。

examples.en: Our class compared purchase decisions for a durable good with decisions about goods used up quickly.
examples.zh: 全班把购买「耐用品」时的决策与购买很快就会用完的商品时的决策作比较。

words.enDefinition: A physical product normally consumed or used up relatively quickly.

examples.en: The classroom catalogue designated printer paper as a nondurable good because the sheets were used up regularly.
examples.zh: 课堂产品目录把打印纸列作「非耐用品」，因为这些纸会经常用完。

examples.en: The fictional shop expected its usual buyers to replace this nondurable good much sooner than a reusable case.
examples.zh: 虚构商店预计熟客补购这件「非耐用品」的频率会比更换可重复使用的外盒高得多。

words.enDefinition: Packaging that immediately contains or directly surrounds the product.

examples.en: The sachet touching the tea leaves counted as primary packaging in the classroom design review.
examples.zh: 直接包着茶叶的小袋在课堂设计评审中算作「内包装」。

examples.en: Our group tested whether the primary packaging could be opened easily without damaging the sample item.
examples.zh: 我们小组测试了能否轻松打开「内包装」，同时不弄坏样品。

words.enDefinition: Packaging that groups or protects one or more already packaged units.

examples.en: The box holding several individually wrapped tea sachets served as secondary packaging in the case.
examples.zh: 案例中，装着多袋独立包装茶叶的盒子充当「外层包装」。

examples.en: We compared secondary packaging that grouped the same units in two differently shaped display boxes.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两类「外层包装」，它们用形状不同的展示盒装相同的独立包装产品。

words.enDefinition: Planning a product's packaging for protection, use, and communication.

examples.en: The package design case compared two closures to see which was easier to reopen after use.
examples.zh: 「包装设计」案例比较两种封口，看看用过之后哪种更容易重新打开。

examples.en: We presented a package design that made the fictional refill easier to recognize on the shelf.
examples.zh: 我们展示了一种「包装设计」，让顾客在货架上更容易认出虚构的补充装。

words.enDefinition: A shared set of components or design elements supporting multiple related products.

examples.en: The two desk organizers shared a product platform but came with different trays and dividers.
examples.zh: 两款桌面收纳架共用一个「产品平台」，但配有不同的托盘和隔板。

examples.en: We included the product platform on the diagram to show which modules the fictional designs shared.
examples.zh: 我们在图中标出「产品平台」，用来展示虚构设计共用的模块。

collocations: build on a shared product platform

words.enDefinition: A model of sales and market development from introduction through decline.

examples.en: We traced the product life cycle of a fictional desk lamp using a chart of annual sales.
examples.zh: 我们用一张年销量图追踪虚构台灯的「产品生命周期」。

examples.en: The reading showed how the product life cycle could differ between two versions of the same item.
examples.zh: 阅读材料说明，同一产品的不同版本，其「产品生命周期」也可能不同。

collocations: stages of the product life cycle

words.enDefinition: The early life-cycle stage when a product first becomes commercially available.

examples.en: The mock catalogue showed the introduction stage beginning when local shops first stocked the new planner.
examples.zh: 模拟目录显示，本地商店开始出售这款新计划本时，就进入了「导入期」。

examples.en: We discussed why sales were initially modest during the introduction stage in the fictional product chart.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么虚构产品图表中的销量在「导入期」初期不高。

words.enDefinition: The life-cycle stage when demand and sales increase relatively quickly.

examples.en: The growth stage started when repeat orders and first purchases rose across the fictional student market.
examples.zh: 在虚构学生市场中，复购订单和首次购买都增多时，产品进入了「成长期」。

examples.en: Our team identified the growth stage by looking for the steepest sustained increase in sales.
examples.zh: 小组通过寻找销量持续上升最快的部分辨认出「成长期」。

collocations: a product in the growth stage

words.enDefinition: The life-cycle stage when sales growth slows as the product becomes established.

examples.en: In the maturity stage, the fictional lamp still sold well, but annual sales barely increased.
examples.zh: 在「成熟期」，虚构台灯依然畅销，但年销量几乎没有增长。

examples.en: We distinguished the maturity stage from decline by checking whether sales had started falling consistently.
examples.zh: 我们核对销量是否已经持续下滑，以区分「成熟期」和衰退期。

collocations: manage a product in the maturity stage

words.enDefinition: The life-cycle stage when sales show a sustained downward trend.

examples.en: The graph marked the decline stage after the fictional calculator's sales fell for three consecutive years.
examples.zh: 图中虚构计算器销量连续三年下降后，这一段被标为「衰退期」。

examples.en: The class discussed whether one unusually slow month was enough to identify the decline stage.
examples.zh: 全班讨论，单凭生意异常清淡的一个月，是否足以判断产品进入「衰退期」。

collocations: manage a product in the decline stage

words.enDefinition: Seeking more buyers or uses for an established product to sustain demand.

examples.en: The fictional planner brand used market modification by offering the existing planner to new campus clubs.
examples.zh: 虚构计划本品牌通过「产品市场拓展」，把原有计划本卖给新的校园社团。

examples.en: We distinguished market modification from redesign because the product stayed exactly the same in the case.
examples.zh: 案例中的产品本身完全没变，因此我们将「产品市场拓展」与重新设计分开讨论。

words.enDefinition: Changing an existing product's features, quality, or design while retaining the offering.

examples.en: The fictional company tried product modification by adding a replaceable handle to its existing mug.
examples.zh: 虚构公司给原有马克杯加上可更换把手，尝试进行「产品改良」。

examples.en: We compared one product modification with the option of introducing an entirely separate desk accessory.
examples.zh: 我们把一项「产品改良」与新推一款独立桌面用品的方案作比较。

words.enDefinition: Updating an existing product line's features or design to reflect current needs.

examples.en: The fictional company began line modernization by updating the oldest designs in its desk lighting range.
examples.zh: 虚构公司从更新台灯系列里最老的设计入手，开始「产品线更新」。

examples.en: Students discussed line modernization because all three existing models looked dated beside the alternatives in the case.
examples.zh: 案例中三种现有型号与备选商品相比都显得过时，学生就此讨论了「产品线更新」。

words.enDefinition: Deliberately limiting a product's useful or desirable life to encourage replacement.

examples.en: The class discussed planned obsolescence when a fictional case described products designed for unusually frequent replacement.
examples.zh: 一个虚构案例提到，产品被刻意设计成需要频繁更换，全班据此讨论了「计划性淘汰」。

examples.en: We asked what evidence would distinguish planned obsolescence from an unintended design flaw in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 我们问，课堂案例中什么证据能将「计划性淘汰」与无心造成的设计缺陷区分开。

words.enDefinition: A new offering taking sales away from another product sold by the same business.

examples.en: The class suspected product cannibalization when the new bag sold well but purchases of its predecessor fell.
examples.zh: 新包袋畅销，但上一款的购买量下降，全班怀疑出现了「自家产品销量蚕食」。

examples.en: We checked combined sales before deciding whether the fictional launch had caused product cannibalization.
examples.zh: 我们先核对合计销量，再判断这次虚构上市是否造成了「自家产品销量蚕食」。

words.enDefinition: Permanently ending the supply of a particular product.

examples.en: The fictional company's product discontinuation notice said it would stop supplying the older model next term.
examples.zh: 虚构公司的「停止供应产品」通知说明，下学期起将不再供应旧型号。

examples.en: Students distinguished product discontinuation from temporarily running out of the item in the fictional store.
examples.zh: 学生区分了「停止供应产品」和虚构商店里该商品暂时售罄。

words.enDefinition: An offering new to any market rather than merely new to its seller.

examples.en: The class asked what evidence would support calling the fictional notebook design a new-to-the-world product.
examples.zh: 全班询问，什么证据能支持把这款虚构笔记本设计称为「全球首创新产品」。

examples.en: The case compared a new-to-the-world product with an existing design offered by another company for years.
examples.zh: 案例将「全球首创新产品」与另一家公司已销售多年的现有设计作比较。

words.zhGloss: 本公司首次推出的产品
words.enDefinition: An offering new to a particular business but already established in the wider market.
acceptedZhAnswers: 本公司首次推出的产品

examples.en: The fictional brand's first desk lamp was a new-to-the-company product in a market with several competitors.
examples.zh: 市场上已有多个竞争者，虚构品牌的首款台灯是「本公司首次推出的产品」。

examples.en: We classified it as a new-to-the-company product because buyers could already find similar products elsewhere.
examples.zh: 我们将它归类为「本公司首次推出的产品」，因为买家早就能从别处找到类似产品。

words.enDefinition: A limited improvement building on an existing product, service, or process.

examples.en: Replacing a difficult closure with an easier one illustrated incremental innovation in the packaging case.
examples.zh: 包装案例用更易开启的封口替代难开的旧款，展示了「渐进式创新」。

examples.en: The assignment traced how incremental innovation gradually improved an established line without changing its central design.
examples.zh: 作业追踪了「渐进式创新」如何逐步改进一条成熟产品线，同时保留其核心设计。

words.enDefinition: An innovation representing a substantial departure from previous products, technologies, or practices.

examples.en: The example counted as radical innovation because the offering met the need in a fundamentally different way.
examples.zh: 这个例子属于「突破式创新」，因为所提供的产品或服务以根本不同的方式满足需求。

examples.en: We debated whether the redesign qualified as radical innovation or simply improved a familiar product concept.
examples.zh: 我们讨论，这次重新设计属于「突破式创新」，还是只是改进了熟悉的产品概念。

collocations: radical innovation in a product category

words.enDefinition: Developing a market offering from its initial idea through preparation for launch.

examples.en: The new product development plan moved from an initial sketch to a trial offering for students.
examples.zh: 「新产品开发」计划从初稿推进到供学生试用的版本。

examples.en: Students mapped new product development to see which decisions came before the fictional item was ready to sell.
examples.zh: 学生绘制「新产品开发」流程图，查看模拟商品上架前需要先作出哪些决定。

collocations: a phase of new product development

words.enDefinition: A development stage evaluating a proposed product's commercial feasibility and likely performance.

examples.en: In the business analysis stage, the fictional team compared its expected expenses with projected notebook sales.
examples.zh: 在「商业分析阶段」，虚构小组将预计开支与笔记本销售预测作比较。

examples.en: We used the business analysis stage to decide whether the concept deserved more project time.
examples.zh: 我们通过「商业分析阶段」判断是否值得在该产品构想上继续投入项目时间。

collocations: findings from the business analysis stage
assess feasibility during the business analysis stage

words.enDefinition: Assessing reactions to a proposed offering before developing or launching the final product.

examples.en: The class used concept testing to compare two proposed bag designs before either existed as a sample.
examples.zh: 课堂用「产品概念测试」比较两款包袋方案，当时两款都还没有样品。

examples.en: Concept testing in the fictional project asked students which benefit they understood from a short description.
examples.zh: 虚构项目的「产品概念测试」询问学生，读过简短描述后理解了产品的哪项好处。

words.enDefinition: Evaluating how a physical or usable version performs under relevant conditions.

examples.en: During product testing, students checked whether the reusable cover still fitted after repeated removal in the simulation.
examples.zh: 在模拟的「产品测试」中，学生检查可重复使用的封皮拆卸多次后是否仍然合适。

examples.en: We compared the product testing notes with earlier opinions about the concept before it had been built.
examples.zh: 我们把「产品测试」记录与实际做出产品前对构想的看法作比较。

words.enDefinition: Offering a product on a limited scale to observe how the market responds.

examples.en: The fictional shop used test marketing at one campus branch before considering a wider launch.
examples.zh: 虚构商店先在一个校区门店进行「试销」，再考虑更大范围上市。

examples.en: We checked whether test marketing measured actual purchases rather than only stated interest in the concept.
examples.zh: 我们核对「试销」是否衡量了实际购买，而不只是顾客口头表达的兴趣。

words.enDefinition: A controlled setting that mimics selected features of a market to study potential buying behavior.

examples.en: The simulated test market showed students several fictional packages before recording which product they would select.
examples.zh: 「模拟试销市场」先向学生展示几个虚构包装，再记录他们会选哪种产品。

examples.en: We compared the simulated test market with sales data from a limited release in local shops.
examples.zh: 我们把「模拟试销市场」与本地商店限量上架得到的销售数据作比较。

collocations: data from a simulated test market
set up a simulated test market

words.enDefinition: Bringing a developed product to market and making it available for purchase.

examples.en: The classroom commercialization plan described how the fictional notebooks would reach customers after development ended.
examples.zh: 课堂上的「商业化投放」方案说明开发完成后，怎样把虚构笔记本卖到顾客手中。

examples.en: We discussed commercialization only after the project team had confirmed that its final product worked.
examples.zh: 项目小组确认成品可用后，我们才讨论「商业化投放」。

words.enDefinition: The spread of an innovation through a population over time.

examples.en: The lecture illustrated the diffusion of innovations by tracing use of a fictional note-sharing tool across campuses.
examples.zh: 老师追踪一款虚构笔记分享工具在不同校园的使用情况，以说明「创新扩散」。

examples.en: We used the diffusion of innovations model to discuss why groups adopted the product at different times.
examples.zh: 我们用「创新扩散」模型讨论，为什么不同群体开始用产品的时间不同。

collocations: a model of the diffusion of innovations
factors affecting the diffusion of innovations

words.enDefinition: An individual or organization's decision to begin using an innovation.

examples.en: The case measured innovation adoption by counting which fictional clubs began using the new storage system.
examples.zh: 案例统计哪些虚构社团开始用新的收纳系统，以衡量「创新采用」。

examples.en: We distinguished innovation adoption from recognizing a product name without using it in the classroom survey.
examples.zh: 我们用课堂问卷区分了「创新采用」与只认得产品名字却没使用的情况。

words.enDefinition: A group classified by when its members adopt an innovation relative to others.

examples.en: The class assigned an adopter category based on when each fictional group first used the product.
examples.zh: 全班按照各虚构群体首次使用产品的时间，将它们归入不同的「采用者类别」。

examples.en: We changed the reference population and checked whether the same participants fell into another adopter category.
examples.zh: 我们更换参照人群，再看相同参与者是否改归另一种「采用者类别」。

collocations: an adopter category in a diffusion model

words.enDefinition: In diffusion theory, the first adopter group to take up an innovation.

examples.en: The fictional innovators were already using the planner while most other students had never seen it.
examples.zh: 虚构的「创新者」开始用这款计划本时，大多数其他学生还没见过它。

examples.en: We marked the innovators at the beginning of the time sequence on the classroom chart.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂图表的时间顺序起点标出了「创新者」。

words.enDefinition: The adopter group following early adopters and preceding the midpoint of adoption in the model.

examples.en: In the simulation, the early majority began using the notebook once the first few groups had adopted it.
examples.zh: 模拟中，最初几个小组采用笔记本后，「早期大众」开始使用它。

examples.en: The class located the early majority before the midpoint on the cumulative chart of fictional adopters.
examples.zh: 在虚构采用者累计图上，全班找到了位于中点之前的「早期大众」。

collocations: the early majority in a diffusion model

words.enDefinition: The adopter group following the midpoint of adoption and preceding the latest adopters in the model.

examples.en: The late majority in the exercise began using the planner after it had become common in the sample.
examples.zh: 练习中，这款计划本在样本人群中已经普及后，「晚期大众」才开始使用。

examples.en: We checked whether the late majority group adopted after the halfway mark in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 我们核对课堂模型里的「晚期大众」是否在累计采用达到一半之后才采用。

collocations: the late majority in a diffusion model

words.enDefinition: In diffusion theory, adopters who take up an innovation latest relative to others.

examples.en: The chart labeled the final adopters as laggards and did not evaluate their reasons for waiting.
examples.zh: 图中将最后采用的人标作「落后者」，也没有评价他们等待的原因。

examples.en: The instructor compared laggards with earlier groups using adoption dates from the fictional notebook launch.
examples.zh: 老师根据虚构笔记本上市后的采用日期，将「落后者」与更早采用的人群作比较。

words.enDefinition: The perceived improvement an innovation offers over the approach it replaces.

examples.en: Easy refilling gave the new notebook a relative advantage over the older model in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 课堂案例中，补充纸页更方便，使新笔记本比旧款具有「创新的相对优势」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the fictional buyers perceived enough relative advantage to switch from the tool they already used.
examples.zh: 我们讨论虚构买家是否察觉到足够的「创新的相对优势」，从而愿意换掉正在用的工具。

words.enDefinition: How well an innovation fits users' needs, values, and existing routines.

examples.en: The example illustrated innovation compatibility because the new pages fitted into the binders students already owned.
examples.zh: 新纸页能装进学生已有的活页夹，示例借此说明「创新相容性」。

examples.en: We examined innovation compatibility with existing classroom routines before comparing the two fictional self-study tools.
examples.zh: 我们先考察新方案与现有课堂习惯的「创新相容性」，再比较两款虚构自学工具。

words.enDefinition: How difficult potential adopters perceive an innovation to understand or use.

examples.en: The simulated buyers reported greater innovation complexity when basic tasks required unfamiliar steps in the new tool.
examples.zh: 新工具的基本操作需要执行不熟悉的步骤时，模拟买家报告其「创新复杂性」更高。

examples.en: The class compared perceived innovation complexity before and after the fictional setup guide was rewritten.
examples.zh: 全班比较虚构入门指南重写前后顾客感受到的「创新复杂性」。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which an innovation can be tried on a limited basis before adoption.

examples.en: The display model improved trialability because students could try one module before choosing the whole kit.
examples.zh: 展示模型提高了「可试用性」，学生可以在选购整套工具之前先试用一个模块。

examples.en: We discussed trialability after comparing two fictional offers that provided different opportunities for hands-on use.
examples.zh: 我们比较了允许不同程度动手体验的两种虚构产品方案，再讨论「可试用性」。

words.enDefinition: How visible the results of using an innovation are to other people.

examples.en: The classroom demonstration increased innovation observability by showing the finished notes produced with the fictional tool.
examples.zh: 课堂演示展示了用虚构工具制作的笔记成品，提高了「创新结果的可观察性」。

examples.en: We discussed innovation observability because the practical benefit was easier to see in a finished example.
examples.zh: 成品示例更容易让人看出实际好处，因此我们讨论了「创新结果的可观察性」。

words.enDefinition: A graph of the total number or share of adopters reached over time.

examples.en: The cumulative adoption curve flattened as fewer new users appeared in the later weeks of the simulation.
examples.zh: 模拟进行到后几周时，新用户变少，「累计采用曲线」趋于平缓。

examples.en: We drew a cumulative adoption curve from the fictional user counts recorded each week on campus.
examples.zh: 我们根据校园中每周记录的虚构用户数画出「累计采用曲线」。

words.enDefinition: The elements and meanings a business deliberately uses to express its brand.

examples.en: The student team kept the same colors and naming rules to make its brand identity consistent.
examples.zh: 学生小组沿用同样的配色和命名规则，让「品牌识别」保持一致。

examples.en: We compared the intended brand identity with the descriptions students gave after seeing the fictional shop.
examples.zh: 我们把预期的「品牌识别」与学生看过虚构商店后给出的描述作比较。

words.enDefinition: The overall set of impressions customers associate with a brand.

examples.en: The interviews suggested a practical brand image even though the fictional shop wanted to feel playful.
examples.zh: 访谈显示，这家虚构商店的「品牌形象」偏实用，而它原本希望给人活泼的感觉。

examples.en: We compared brand image across two campus locations that showed the same sign and product names.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个校区顾客心中的「品牌形象」，两处使用同样的招牌和产品名称。

words.enDefinition: A brand representing the organization as a whole across offerings and audiences.

examples.en: The fictional stationery company's corporate brand appeared on its hiring pages and public reports as well as packaging.
examples.zh: 虚构文具公司的「企业品牌」既出现在包装上，也出现在招聘页面和公开报告中。

examples.en: We distinguished the corporate brand from the separate name on one line of notebooks in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们区分了「企业品牌」和单独印在一个笔记本系列上的名称。

collocations: the reputation of a corporate brand

words.enDefinition: A brand identifying a specific product or line of products.

examples.en: The mock company gave its new desk lamp a product brand separate from its corporate name.
examples.zh: 模拟公司为新台灯取了一个独立于公司名称的「产品品牌」。

examples.en: The case used a different product brand for each of two bags made by the same firm.
examples.zh: 案例中，同一家公司生产两款包袋，每款各用一个「产品品牌」。

words.enDefinition: A brand identifying an ongoing service or a provider's service experience.

examples.en: Our case gave the bicycle lending program a service brand that appeared on signs and reservation screens.
examples.zh: 我们的案例为自行车借用计划设定了一个「服务品牌」，用在标牌和预约界面上。

examples.en: We discussed how the service brand helped students recognize the fictional tutoring service across different locations.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「服务品牌」如何帮助学生在不同地点认出该虚构辅导服务。

words.enDefinition: A brand owned or controlled by a retailer and sold as its own offering.

examples.en: The fictional bookstore sold basic pens under a private-label brand carrying the shop's own name.
examples.zh: 虚构书店用印有自身名称的「零售商自有品牌」销售基础款笔。

examples.en: We compared a private-label brand with products sold under their manufacturers' names in the same shop.
examples.zh: 我们把一种「零售商自有品牌」与同店以生产商自己名义销售的产品作比较。

words.enDefinition: A brand owned by a manufacturer and marketed under its own identity.

examples.en: The notebooks carried a manufacturer brand that appeared in several fictional shops under the same name.
examples.zh: 这些笔记本使用一个「制造商自有品牌」，在多家虚构商店以同名销售。

examples.en: We discussed why the producer sold some pencils under a manufacturer brand and others under retailer names.
examples.zh: 我们讨论为什么该生产商有时以「制造商自有品牌」售卖铅笔，有时用零售商的名称。

collocations: compare a manufacturer brand with a store brand

words.enDefinition: The verbal label by which customers identify and refer to a brand.

examples.en: The group chose a brand name that students could pronounce after seeing it for the first time.
examples.zh: 小组选了一个学生第一次看到就能念出的「品牌名称」。

examples.en: We checked whether the fictional stationery shop used the same brand name on its products and receipts.
examples.zh: 我们核对虚构文具店是否在产品和收据上使用同一个「品牌名称」。

words.enDefinition: A recognizable visual symbol associated with a brand, apart from its spoken name.

examples.en: The small geometric brand mark remained recognizable even on the narrow side of the reusable notebook.
examples.zh: 即使印在可重复使用的笔记本窄侧边，小小的几何「品牌图形标识」也能认出。

examples.en: We checked whether students could match the brand mark to the fictional shop without seeing its name.
examples.zh: 我们看学生在看不到店名时，能否把「品牌图形标识」与虚构商店对应起来。

words.enDefinition: Human traits that customers associate with a brand.

examples.en: The class described the fictional brand personality as friendly because its packaging and store signs felt approachable.
examples.zh: 全班觉得这家虚构品牌的包装和店内标牌让人容易亲近，认为其「品牌个性」偏友好。

examples.en: We compared brand personality across two fictional brands that offered similarly practical products for students.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个虚构品牌的「品牌个性」，它们都为学生提供同样实用的产品。

words.enDefinition: A logo formed primarily from the stylized written name of a brand.

examples.en: The new wordmark used only the fictional brand's name in a distinctive style of lettering.
examples.zh: 新的「品牌文字标识」只用虚构品牌的名字，通过独特字形表现出来。

examples.en: We compared the wordmark with the icon that could appear on its own in smaller spaces.
examples.zh: 我们把「品牌文字标识」与可在狭小位置独立使用的图标作比较。

words.enDefinition: An organized set of visual elements used consistently to identify a brand.

examples.en: The fictional campus store used one visual identity system across labels, shelf signs, and its online catalogue.
examples.zh: 虚构校园商店在标签、货架标牌和在线目录上使用统一的「视觉识别系统」。

examples.en: The project team assembled a visual identity system using a shared typeface, palette, and set of shapes.
examples.zh: 项目小组用统一的字体、色板和一组图形组成「视觉识别系统」。

words.enDefinition: Rules explaining how to present a brand consistently across materials and settings.

examples.en: Our team checked the brand guidelines before placing the fictional shop's mark on the packaging mockup.
examples.zh: 小组在把虚构商店的标识放到包装样稿前，先查阅了「品牌使用规范」。

examples.en: The brand guidelines explained which colors and typefaces could appear together on the product card.
examples.zh: 「品牌使用规范」说明了哪些颜色和字体可以搭配出现在产品卡上。

words.enDefinition: The system organizing roles and relationships among a company's brands and offerings.

examples.en: The brand architecture chart showed why some product lines shared a name while others used separate names.
examples.zh: 「品牌架构」图说明了为什么有些产品线共用名称，有些另用名称。

examples.en: We revised the brand architecture after the fictional company added a product for a different audience.
examples.zh: 虚构公司增加了一款面向不同受众的产品后，我们修改了「品牌架构」。

words.enDefinition: A structure in which most offerings share a single prominent master brand.

examples.en: Under a branded house, the fictional company sold notebooks and lamps under the same visible name.
examples.zh: 采用「统一主品牌架构」时，虚构公司用同一个显眼的名称销售笔记本和台灯。

examples.en: The branded house case kept the main name large while giving each offering a brief descriptor.
examples.zh: 「统一主品牌架构」案例中，主品牌名称保留大字样，同时为每项产品加上简短的描述。

words.enDefinition: A structure in which a company owns several brands with distinct market identities.

examples.en: The fictional parent company used a house of brands so customers rarely saw its corporate name.
examples.zh: 虚构母公司采用「多独立品牌架构」，所以顾客很少看到其企业名称。

examples.en: The house of brands chart linked each fictional stationery brand to the same owner at the top.
examples.zh: 「多独立品牌架构」图将各个虚构文具品牌连接到顶端的同一个所有者。

collocations: operate as a house of brands

words.enDefinition: A distinct brand whose credibility is visibly supported by another brand.

examples.en: The fictional shop treated its notebook label as an endorsed brand by placing its company name below.
examples.zh: 虚构商店在笔记本品牌下方标上公司名称，使其成为「背书式品牌」。

examples.en: Students separated the endorsed brand's name from the small supporting name printed beside it in the example.
examples.zh: 学生区分了示例中的「背书式品牌」名称和印在旁边字号较小的背书方名称。

collocations: display the parent name on an endorsed brand

words.enDefinition: A distinct identity linked closely to a master brand and modifying its meaning for particular offerings.

examples.en: The fictional master brand added a study sub-brand while keeping its main name prominent on the packaging.
examples.zh: 虚构主品牌增设了一个学习用品「子品牌」，包装仍突出主品牌名称。

examples.en: Our chart showed how the sub-brand appealed to students while still clearly belonging to the master brand.
examples.zh: 我们的图说明「子品牌」如何吸引学生，同时仍明确隶属于主品牌。

collocations: connect a sub-brand with its master brand

words.enDefinition: The dominant brand name shared across several related products, services, or sub-brands.

examples.en: The team placed the masterbrand on every package, then added a short name for each product line.
examples.zh: 小组将「主品牌」印在所有包装上，再为各产品线加上简短名称。

examples.en: We mapped which fictional offerings shared the masterbrand and which carried unrelated names in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们绘图注明哪些虚构产品共用「主品牌」，哪些使用彼此无关的名称。

collocations: link an offering to the masterbrand

words.enDefinition: A brand with a distinct public identity and little visible connection to its owner or sister brands.

examples.en: The fictional company sold lamps under a standalone brand with no parent name on the box.
examples.zh: 虚构公司以「独立品牌」销售台灯，包装盒上没有母公司名称。

examples.en: We asked whether the new line should share the main name or become a standalone brand.
examples.zh: 我们讨论新产品线应当沿用主名称，还是成为一个「独立品牌」。

collocations: market an offering as a standalone brand

words.enDefinition: The collection of brands an organization owns or manages.

examples.en: The fictional company's brand portfolio contained three labels serving different needs in the campus stationery market.
examples.zh: 虚构公司的「品牌组合」里有三个品牌，满足校园文具市场的不同需求。

examples.en: Our group reviewed the brand portfolio to see whether two of its labels addressed the same use.
examples.zh: 小组梳理了「品牌组合」，查看其中两个品牌所满足的用途是否相同。

words.enDefinition: The ordering of brand names from broader levels to more specific levels.

examples.en: The brand hierarchy diagram started with the fictional company name and ended with individual model names.
examples.zh: 「品牌层级」图从虚构公司名称开始，最后细分到各个型号名称。

examples.en: We checked where the line name belonged in the brand hierarchy on the sample package.
examples.zh: 我们核对样品包装上的系列名称在「品牌层级」中应放在哪一层。

collocations: a level of the brand hierarchy

words.enDefinition: An existing brand whose name or reputation supports an extension or related brand.

examples.en: Buyers in the case recognized the parent brand even though they had never seen the new product.
examples.zh: 尽管从未见过这款新产品，案例中的买家还是认出了「母品牌」。

examples.en: We identified the parent brand before discussing whether its association with durability would transfer to the extension.
examples.zh: 我们先辨认出「母品牌」，再讨论顾客对它的耐用印象能否转移到延伸产品上。

collocations: a link to the parent brand

words.enDefinition: Using an established brand name for an offering in a different product category.

examples.en: The fictional notebook company tried a brand extension by selling study lamps under its existing name.
examples.zh: 虚构笔记本公司用原有品牌名销售学习台灯，尝试「跨品类品牌延伸」。

examples.en: Our team evaluated whether buyers would understand why the brand extension belonged with the original notebooks.
examples.zh: 小组评估买家是否理解，为什么「跨品类品牌延伸」产品适合与原有笔记本共用品牌。

words.enDefinition: Using an existing brand name for a new variant in its current category.

examples.en: The unscented soap was a line extension because the fictional brand already sold several scented versions.
examples.zh: 虚构品牌本来就销售多个有香味的肥皂款式，因此无香款属于「同品类品牌延伸」。

examples.en: We proposed a line extension using the same notebook name for a new page layout.
examples.zh: 我们建议沿用笔记本原来的名称，推出新版内页布局，作为「同品类品牌延伸」。

words.enDefinition: How naturally customers think a proposed extension fits its established brand.

examples.en: Students rated extension fit higher when the new product served a familiar purpose for that brand.
examples.zh: 新产品满足的是该品牌原先就让人熟悉的用途时，学生给出的「品牌延伸契合度」评分更高。

examples.en: The case discussed extension fit before comparing customer reactions to the two fictional proposals.
examples.zh: 在比较顾客对两个虚构方案的反应之前，案例先讨论了「品牌延伸契合度」。

words.enDefinition: Weakening of established brand associations when a brand is used inconsistently or too broadly.

examples.en: The team worried about brand dilution after the fictional label appeared on many unrelated products.
examples.zh: 这个虚构品牌出现在许多互不相干的产品上后，团队担心出现「品牌联想淡化」。

examples.en: We looked for brand dilution by comparing what customers associated with the name across two fictional surveys.
examples.zh: 我们对照两份虚构调查中顾客对该名称的联想，看看是否出现「品牌联想淡化」。

words.enDefinition: Efforts to renew relevance and demand for an established brand losing momentum.

examples.en: The fictional stationery line began brand revitalization after students described it as familiar but outdated.
examples.zh: 学生形容这个虚构文具系列虽然熟悉但显得过时，系列由此开始「品牌活化」。

examples.en: Our case compared two brand revitalization proposals that preserved different aspects of the original brand.
examples.zh: 案例比较了两项「品牌活化」方案，它们各自保留了原品牌的不同方面。

words.enDefinition: A limited update to a brand's presentation that retains its main identity.

examples.en: The brand refresh introduced clearer packaging while keeping the name and core associations customers already recognized.
examples.zh: 「品牌形象更新」带来了更清晰的包装，同时保留顾客已熟悉的名称和核心联想。

examples.en: We designed a brand refresh for the fictional shop by updating its colors and leaving its name unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们为虚构商店设计了一次「品牌形象更新」，更新配色，同时保留店名。

words.enDefinition: A substantial change to an established brand's name, identity, or public presentation.

examples.en: The fictional store considered rebranding after deciding its old name no longer represented the wider product selection.
examples.zh: 虚构商店认为旧名称已不能代表其更丰富的产品，于是考虑「品牌重塑」。

examples.en: We compared a limited design update with rebranding that would replace the shop's existing name entirely.
examples.zh: 我们将有限的设计更新与彻底替换原店名的「品牌重塑」作比较。

words.enDefinition: Using two established brand names together on one product or service.

examples.en: The classroom case showed co-branding when two student ventures put their names on a shared kit.
examples.zh: 课堂案例中，两家学生创业团队把各自的名称印在同一个套装上，展示了「联合品牌」。

examples.en: We checked whether the co-branding made both fictional product names easy to recognize on the package.
examples.zh: 我们查看在这种「联合品牌」安排下，顾客是否能轻松认出包装上的两个虚构品牌名称。

words.enDefinition: Highlighting a separately branded component or ingredient as part of a finished product.

examples.en: The fictional bag used ingredient branding by identifying its fabric with a separately recognizable supplier's mark.
examples.zh: 虚构包袋用可单独辨认的供应商品牌标明布料，采用了「成分品牌化」。

examples.en: We discussed ingredient branding when the notebook maker featured a distinct paper brand on the package.
examples.zh: 笔记本制造商在包装上突出显示一个单独的纸张品牌时，我们讨论了「成分品牌化」。

words.enDefinition: Permission for another organization to use a brand under agreed terms.

examples.en: The fictional manufacturer used brand licensing to put an established campus shop name on its desk accessories.
examples.zh: 虚构制造商通过「品牌授权」在桌面用品上使用现有校园商店名称。

examples.en: We distinguished brand licensing from a case in which a retailer acquired the brand outright.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「品牌授权」与零售商直接买下该品牌的情况。

words.enDefinition: The added marketplace value an offering gains from its brand name and associations.

examples.en: In the classroom case, strong brand equity helped the fictional notebook stand apart from nearly identical alternatives.
examples.zh: 课堂案例中，较强的「品牌资产」让虚构笔记本有别于几乎一样的备选商品。

examples.en: We discussed how brand equity might be affected if familiar products no longer matched customer expectations.
examples.zh: 我们讨论，如果熟悉的产品已不符合顾客预期，「品牌资产」会受到怎样的影响。

words.enDefinition: An estimate of a brand's monetary worth under a stated valuation approach.

examples.en: The fictional report expressed brand value in money and clearly described the assumptions behind the estimate.
examples.zh: 虚构报告以货币表示「品牌货币价值」，并清楚说明估值所依据的假设。

examples.en: We distinguished brand value from the percentages of students who recognized the fictional brand in the survey.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「品牌货币价值」和问卷中能认出虚构品牌的学生比例。

words.enDefinition: The difference in customer response attributable to what they know about a brand.

examples.en: The case compared responses to identical products with and without names to illustrate customer-based brand equity.
examples.zh: 案例比较了受众对同一款产品在有无品牌名时的反应，以说明「顾客视角的品牌资产」。

examples.en: We discussed customer-based brand equity when students judged two identical fictional offers differently after seeing their names.
examples.zh: 学生看见名称后对两个完全相同的虚构产品作出不同评价，我们就此讨论了「顾客视角的品牌资产」。

collocations: a model of customer-based brand equity

words.enDefinition: A lasting preference or commitment that can lead customers to keep choosing a brand.

examples.en: The fictional survey measured brand loyalty by asking whether buyers would stick with the same brand.
examples.zh: 虚构问卷通过询问买家是否会继续选择同一个品牌，衡量「品牌忠诚度」。

examples.en: We discussed whether repeat purchases showed brand loyalty when students had very few other options on campus.
examples.zh: 我们讨论，当学生在校内几乎没有其他选项时，重复购买是否体现了「品牌忠诚度」。

words.enDefinition: How well potential customers can recognize or remember a brand.

examples.en: Brand awareness increased in the fictional survey when more students recognized the stationery label shown in class.
examples.zh: 在虚构问卷中，更多学生认出课堂上展示的文具品牌，「品牌知晓度」有所提高。

examples.en: Our team measured brand awareness before asking which qualities participants associated with each fictional brand.
examples.zh: 小组先测量「品牌知晓度」，再问参与者把哪些特征与各虚构品牌联系起来。

words.enDefinition: Identifying a brand after seeing or hearing its name or another cue.

examples.en: The brand recognition exercise showed several names and asked which ones students had seen before.
examples.zh: 「品牌再认」练习展示了几个名称，问学生此前见过哪些。

examples.en: We compared brand recognition for the fictional store's name and its symbol in the classroom survey.
examples.zh: 在课堂问卷中，我们比较了虚构商店的名称和图形标识各自的「品牌再认」表现。

words.enDefinition: Retrieving a brand name from memory, often in response to a product category or shopping situation.

examples.en: To test brand recall, the instructor named a product category and asked students to list familiar brands.
examples.zh: 为了测试「品牌回忆」，老师说出一个产品品类，请学生列出熟悉的品牌。

examples.en: We compared brand recall with the results from a separate question that showed each fictional name.
examples.zh: 我们把「品牌回忆」与另一个显示各虚构品牌名称的问题所得结果作比较。

words.enDefinition: In brand surveys, the share of respondents who name a brand first when asked to recall brands in its category.

examples.en: The student team measured top-of-mind awareness by counting which label respondents named first in each category.
examples.zh: 学生小组统计回答者在每个品类首先说出的品牌，以测量「品牌第一提及率」。

examples.en: The fictional brand had high overall recognition but low top-of-mind awareness in the classroom comparison.
examples.zh: 课堂比较中，这个虚构品牌的整体再认表现不错，但「品牌第一提及率」较低。

words.enDefinition: How readily a brand comes to mind in relevant buying or usage situations.

examples.en: The case explored brand salience by asking which name came to mind when a desk lamp stopped working.
examples.zh: 案例询问台灯坏了时大家会想到哪个品牌，以考察「品牌显著性」。

examples.en: We compared brand salience across situations where fictional students had different reasons to buy stationery.
examples.zh: 我们比较虚构学生因不同目的购买文具时，各情境下的「品牌显著性」。

collocations: brand salience in a purchase situation

words.enDefinition: The ideas, feelings, or images customers link to a brand in memory.

examples.en: The exercise identified brand associations when students linked the fictional notebook label with plain, durable designs.
examples.zh: 在练习中，学生把虚构笔记本品牌与简洁耐用的设计联系起来，显示了「品牌联想」。

examples.en: We compared the brand associations for two names that students recognized equally often in the example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，学生认出两个名称的频率相同，我们对比了他们各自的「品牌联想」。

words.enDefinition: Associations concerning the people, situations, and symbolic meanings connected with a brand.

examples.en: The fictional survey captured brand imagery when students associated the notebook with sketching outdoors on weekends.
examples.zh: 学生将这款笔记本和周末在户外速写联系起来，虚构问卷记录了这种「品牌象征性联想」。

examples.en: We examined brand imagery separately from how buyers judged the strength of the notebook's paper.
examples.zh: 我们将「品牌象征性联想」与买家对笔记本纸张强韧度的评价分开考察。

words.enDefinition: A deep customer bond expressed through strong attachment and active engagement with a brand.

examples.en: The class discussed brand resonance after fictional customers kept choosing the brand and also joined its user community.
examples.zh: 虚构顾客持续选择该品牌，还加入了它的用户社群，全班借此讨论了「品牌共鸣」。

examples.en: We compared brand resonance with simply knowing the fictional name from seeing it on a shelf.
examples.zh: 我们把「品牌共鸣」与仅因在货架上见过而认得虚构品牌名称的情况作比较。

words.enDefinition: Defining a product's intended place in customers' minds relative to alternatives.

examples.en: Our product positioning emphasized the compact size of this lamp for students with small shared desks.
examples.zh: 我们的「产品定位」强调这款台灯体积小，适合合用小书桌的学生。

examples.en: We revised the product positioning after classmates described the fictional bag as practical for everyday use.
examples.zh: 同学认为虚构包袋适合日常使用后，我们修改了「产品定位」。

words.enDefinition: Defining how a brand should be perceived relative to competitors across its offerings.

examples.en: The team's brand positioning emphasized practical stationery across notebooks, pencil cases, and other classroom supplies.
examples.zh: 小组的「品牌定位」突出实用文具，涵盖笔记本、笔袋及其他课堂用品。

examples.en: We checked whether the fictional brand positioning still made sense when the company added desk accessories.
examples.zh: 我们核对公司新增了桌面用品后，虚构的「品牌定位」是否仍然合适。

words.enDefinition: Changing a brand's intended relative place in the minds of its target customers.

examples.en: The case discussed brand repositioning when the fictional shop shifted from novelty gifts to practical study supplies.
examples.zh: 虚构商店从新奇礼品转向实用学习用品时，案例讨论了「品牌重新定位」。

examples.en: We compared brand repositioning with changing the logo while keeping the same intended customers and benefits.
examples.zh: 我们将「品牌重新定位」与只换标识、保留目标顾客与主打利益的做法作比较。

words.enDefinition: The category or alternatives against which customers are meant to evaluate the brand.

examples.en: Our competitive frame of reference included ordinary desk organizers because students compared the new item with them.
examples.zh: 学生用普通桌面收纳架与新品比较，所以我们的「竞争参照框架」涵盖了这类收纳架。

examples.en: The instructor asked whether the competitive frame of reference should include both shared storage and portable cases.
examples.zh: 老师问，「竞争参照框架」是否应同时包含共享收纳设施和便携收纳盒。

collocations: define the competitive frame of reference
select a competitive frame of reference
change the competitive frame of reference

words.enDefinition: The specific set of competitors used for a market or positioning comparison.

examples.en: We built a competitive set from the three desk accessory brands mentioned most often by fictional buyers.
examples.zh: 我们取虚构买家最常提到的三个桌面用品品牌，组成「竞争品牌参照组」。

examples.en: The competitive set changed after our case moved from campus bookstores to shops with broader assortments.
examples.zh: 案例所考察的店从校园书店换成品类更多的商店后，「竞争品牌参照组」也变了。

collocations: compare brands in a competitive set

words.enDefinition: A business or product offering a closely comparable solution to the same customers.

examples.en: The second notebook maker was a direct competitor because it sold a similar product to campus buyers.
examples.zh: 第二家笔记本制造商向校园买家卖类似商品，因此是「直接竞争者」。

examples.en: We included a direct competitor on the map to show how buyers compared two reusable planners.
examples.zh: 我们在图上纳入一家「直接竞争者」，展示买家如何比较两款可重复使用的计划本。

words.enDefinition: A business or product meeting the same customer need in a different way.

examples.en: In the exercise, the scheduling app was an indirect competitor to the fictional paper planner.
examples.zh: 在练习中，日程管理应用是这款虚构纸质计划本的「间接竞争者」。

examples.en: We discussed the bike rental club as an indirect competitor to the fictional secondhand bicycle shop.
examples.zh: 我们把自行车租借社团视为虚构二手自行车店的「间接竞争者」来讨论。

collocations: distinguish an indirect competitor from a direct one

words.enDefinition: An attribute or benefit customers consider necessary for an offering to belong to a category.

examples.en: In the case, stable placement on a flat surface was a category point of parity for desk lamps.
examples.zh: 案例中，在平面上放置稳固是台灯应具备的一个「品类共同点」。

examples.en: The class treated a secure fastening as a category point of parity for the fictional backpack line.
examples.zh: 全班把能扣牢的搭扣视为虚构双肩包产品系列的一项「品类共同点」。

collocations: establish a category point of parity
identify a category point of parity
category point of parity for new entrants

words.enDefinition: An attribute or benefit matching a competitor closely enough to neutralize its advantage.

examples.en: The fictional shop added a similar repair service to establish a competitive point of parity with its rival.
examples.zh: 虚构商店增设了相似的维修服务，与对手形成一项「竞争对等点」。

examples.en: We identified a competitive point of parity when both fictional brands offered the same useful replacement feature.
examples.zh: 两个虚构品牌都提供同一种实用的替换功能时，我们找出了一项「竞争对等点」。

collocations: establish a competitive point of parity
a competitive point of parity on reliability
identify a competitive point of parity

words.enDefinition: An association or benefit a brand shares with other credible offerings in its competitive context.

examples.en: Both fictional stationery brands offered spare covers, so the worksheet marked this as a point of parity.
examples.zh: 两个虚构文具品牌都供应备用封皮，所以习题把这一点标为「对等点」。

examples.en: We identified a point of parity before discussing which features actually made the new planner distinctive.
examples.zh: 我们先找出一个「对等点」，再讨论哪些功能真正让这款新计划本与众不同。

words.enDefinition: A relevant attribute or benefit customers strongly associate with one brand over competitors.

examples.en: The replaceable cover gave the fictional notebook a point of difference because comparable brands offered fixed covers.
examples.zh: 类似品牌都提供固定封皮，可更换封皮因此成了虚构笔记本的一个「差异点」。

examples.en: We tested whether the proposed point of difference mattered to students before using it in the assignment.
examples.zh: 我们先了解提出的「差异点」对学生是否重要，再把它写进作业。

words.enDefinition: A consistent benefit or experience a brand commits to providing to customers.

examples.en: The fictional store's brand promise was that students could find basic supplies quickly during class breaks.
examples.zh: 虚构商店的「品牌承诺」是让学生在课间快速找到基础学习用品。

examples.en: We checked whether the new catalogue still supported the brand promise of making study supplies easy to find.
examples.zh: 我们核对新目录是否仍能兑现让学习用品容易找的「品牌承诺」。

words.enDefinition: A short internal phrase guiding decisions by expressing what the brand fundamentally stands for.

examples.en: The team used a brand mantra to judge whether a new accessory belonged under the fictional name.
examples.zh: 小组用「品牌内部信条」判断某款新配件是否适合用虚构品牌的名称。

examples.en: We compared the brand mantra with the longer positioning statement used in the classroom planning exercise.
examples.zh: 我们把「品牌内部信条」和课堂策划练习中篇幅更长的定位陈述作比较。

words.enDefinition: The central meaning or idea that gives a brand its enduring character.

examples.en: The workshop identified simple organization as the brand essence behind the fictional range of classroom supplies.
examples.zh: 工作坊将简单有序确定为这个虚构课堂用品系列背后的「品牌精髓」。

examples.en: We checked whether the proposed lamps reflected the same brand essence as the shop's original notebooks.
examples.zh: 我们核对计划推出的台灯是否体现了与店铺原有笔记本相同的「品牌精髓」。

words.enDefinition: A concise description of an offering's target customers, competitive context, and distinct value.

examples.en: Our positioning statement described who needed the compact lamp and what made it different from comparable models.
examples.zh: 我们的「定位陈述」说明了谁需要这款小台灯，以及它有别于类似型号的地方。

examples.en: We read the positioning statement aloud to see whether it made the intended benefit clear.
examples.zh: 我们大声读出「定位陈述」，看它是否说清了主打的利益。

words.enDefinition: A diagram showing how customers perceive competing offerings along selected dimensions.

examples.en: The team placed each fictional brand on a perceptual map of durability and ease of carrying.
examples.zh: 小组把每个虚构品牌标在以耐用性和便携性为维度的「知觉定位图」上。

examples.en: We read the perceptual map to see which two product lines were perceived as most alike.
examples.zh: 我们解读「知觉定位图」，查看顾客认为哪两条产品线最相似。

collocations: plot brands on a perceptual map

words.enDefinition: A product characteristic that meaningfully influences buyers' choice among competing options.

examples.en: Easy carrying became a determinant attribute once students chose repeatedly between cases of different weights.
examples.zh: 学生在不同重量的收纳盒中反复作选择时，便携性成为一项「决定性产品属性」。

examples.en: We tested whether color was a determinant attribute or merely something students liked in all versions.
examples.zh: 我们测试颜色究竟是「决定性产品属性」，还是仅仅在各个版本里都受学生喜欢。

collocations: compare offers on a determinant attribute

words.enDefinition: Positioning an offering directly against established rivals on comparable attributes or benefits.

examples.en: Our head-to-head positioning compared the fictional planner with rivals on layout, durability, and ease of use.
examples.zh: 我们的「正面竞争定位」将虚构计划本与竞争商品在布局、耐用性和易用性上作比较。

examples.en: The case illustrated head-to-head positioning by comparing two nearly identical notebooks on the same features.
examples.zh: 案例对照两个极为相似的笔记本的同类功能，说明了「正面竞争定位」。

words.enDefinition: Positioning an offering around a distinctive quality or benefit customers value.

examples.en: The project used differentiation positioning by presenting the fictional notebook as especially suited to sketches and diagrams.
examples.zh: 项目采用「差异化定位」，将虚构笔记本定位为特别适合速写和画示意图的产品。

examples.en: We chose differentiation positioning after finding that rivals all emphasized the same familiar study features.
examples.zh: 发现竞争产品都突出同样常见的学习功能后，我们选择了「差异化定位」。

words.enDefinition: Positioning an offering around a specific characteristic it possesses.

examples.en: The fictional shop used attribute positioning by highlighting the desk lamp's rotating head in the case.
examples.zh: 案例中的虚构商店采取「基于属性的定位」，突出台灯可旋转的灯头。

examples.en: We compared attribute positioning for two bags that emphasized different materials in their product descriptions.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两款包袋的「基于属性的定位」，它们在产品描述中强调不同材料。

collocations: position a product through attribute positioning

words.enDefinition: Positioning an offering around an outcome customers gain from using it.

examples.en: The case used benefit positioning by focusing on how quickly students could clear their desks after studying.
examples.zh: 案例采用「基于利益的定位」，突出学生学习结束后能多快收拾好桌面。

examples.en: We chose benefit positioning for the fictional lamp because the class valued saving space more than design details.
examples.zh: 我们为虚构台灯选择「基于利益的定位」，因为全班比起设计细节更重视节省空间。

words.enDefinition: Positioning an offering around a particular situation or occasion for its use.

examples.en: The fictional brand tried use-occasion positioning by presenting the small kit as useful during short library visits.
examples.zh: 虚构品牌尝试「基于使用场合的定位」，强调这套小工具适合在图书馆短暂停留时使用。

examples.en: We compared use-occasion positioning for an everyday bag with a plan centered on weekend trips.
examples.zh: 我们把日常用包的「基于使用场合的定位」，与以周末短途出行为重点的方案作比较。
